title: MA2H Inbound Entry (v0.5)
description: Hub->Agent delivered mailbox entry payload (spec §8.7, §13). v0.4 delivered a single kind — the human->agent `directive`. v0.5 adds three entry kinds, delivered ONLY to session-presenting drains (spec §8.7): `message` (an addressed §4 envelope, agent-authored notify/ask/task, with Hub-assigned `id` and Hub-attested `from`), `response` (a §6 Response delivered to the submitting session's mailbox), and `receipt` (a Hub-originated delivery-status notification to a sender). Each drained entry pairs its payload with a detached signature — `{ "directive"|"message"|"response"|"receipt": <payload>, "signature": ... }` — signed per spec §9.7 (directive) or §9.8 (v0.5 entry kinds), re-signed with a fresh t/jti at each delivery. This schema validates the delivered PAYLOAD (any of the four kinds); a consuming agent MUST validate the payload shape before acting (spec §13.4), because the payload digests bind only content fields — an on-path injector can add unsigned fields without breaking the signature.

directive.title: directive (human->agent, v0.4)
directive.description: The DELIVERED form of a human->agent directive (spec §13.1): `id` and `from` are Hub-assigned/attested, never agent- or request-supplied. No `request`/`action` (human->agent ask/task is deferred) and no `state` (not an agent-owned resume blob).

ma2h_version.description: Directives are a v0.4 feature; the minor MUST be >= 4 (a pre-0.4 recipient would not know the §9.7 signature/addressee semantics).

id.description: Hub-assigned canonical directive id. The agent's at-most-once dedup key.

from.description: Hub-attested author (never request-supplied). `human:<id>`; `system:<id>` reserved for Hub-originated directives.

to.description: Addressed agent (`agent:<id>`, or `agent:<id>#<session>` for a session-addressed directive, v0.5 spec §13.2); the mailbox routing key. The §4 first-`#` grammar applies to directives too (spec §13.2, retroactive destination validation): the session segment must match ^sess_.

body.description: Human-authored Markdown detail. UNTRUSTED agent input (the inbound mirror of §9.6): a directive drives agent behavior, so treat it as a prompt-/command-injection surface until the signature is verified.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339. After this the Hub stops delivering and drops the directive (no response leg). MUST be in the future at author time.

sensitive.description: Message-level sensitivity; excludes value(s) from export/telemetry.

interAgentMessage.title: message (agent->agent, v0.5)
interAgentMessage.description: The DELIVERED form of an addressed §4 envelope (spec §8.7): the submitted notify/ask/task plus Hub-assigned `id` and Hub-attested `from` (`agent:<id>`, session-qualified when the submit carried `agent.session`). The Hub strips submitter-side machinery before delivery — `state` (the submitter's opaque resume blob, round-tripped only in the §6 Response), `client_ref` (§9.1 forbids exposing it to resolvers), and any `request.callback`/`action.callback` (the submitter's delivery config) — and this branch FORBIDS them so a consuming agent's shape validation rejects unsigned injected copies (they are outside the §9.8 payload digest). The `agent` descriptor is delivered but ADVISORY (unbound, like §9.2's top-level agent); the attested identity is `from`.

ma2h_version.description: Inter-agent message entries are a v0.5 feature; the minor MUST be >= 5.

id.description: Hub-assigned canonical message id. The recipient's at-most-once dedup key (spec §13.4 applied wholesale).

from.description: Hub-attested submitter (never request-supplied): `agent:<id>`, session-qualified when the submit carried `agent.session`.

responseEntry.title: response (Hub->submitting session, v0.5)
responseEntry.description: A §6 Response delivered as a mailbox entry to the submitting session (spec §8.7): the return leg for an agent-addressed ask/task, and available to any session-registered Caller in place of a webhook. The Response body is byte-for-byte the v0.4 shape; the delivery destination is bound only in the §9.8 signed context (`to`), which the drainer reconstructs from its own presented identity. Enqueued only when the submitting session is live at resolution time; otherwise delivery falls back to the unchanged §8.2 pull / §8.3 callback with no bounce. Dedup on (in_reply_to, resolution_id).

receipt.title: receipt (Hub->sender, v0.5)
receipt.description: A Hub-originated delivery-status notification to a SENDER (spec §8.7, §14.2): v0.5 uses it for the bounce. Best-effort, at-most-once-meaningful — the recipient dedups on (in_reply_to, event) — delivered only to live sessions of the sender, and a receipt MUST NOT itself generate receipts. The sender's §8.2 pull remains authoritative.

ma2h_version.description: Receipt entries are a v0.5 feature; the minor MUST be >= 5.

id.description: Hub-assigned receipt id — this entry's ack key (spec §8.7.1) and part of the §9.8 digest, so the key a consumer acks is signature-bound. Distinct from the dedup pair (in_reply_to, event).

in_reply_to.description: The affected entry/message id — also the dedup key together with `event`.

event.description: The delivery-track event this receipt reports. `bounced` in v0.5; future minors may add events.

prior.description: The delivery-track state the entry bounced FROM: `queued` = never seen; `delivered` = drained-but-unacked when the destination session went terminal (seen-then-orphaned, spec §14.2).

session.description: The terminal destination session whose death bounced the entry.

to.description: The sender session this receipt is delivered to (receipts are delivered only to live sender sessions); bound in the §9.8 signed context against cross-destination replay, and checked by the recipient like every entry's addressee (spec §13.4).
